name: lab_state
description: Read a network-xray lab state (read-only) and summarize it: nodes and interfaces, links, OSPF adjacencies, BGP sessions and counts. No router is contacted.

path.description: A state_<node>.json, a directory of them, an xray-states.js, or a directory of saved FRR show ... json files

name: why_best_path
description: For one node and prefix, give the BGP best path and the reason stored in the data (FRR selectionReason, or the IOS-XE collector's derived reason). If the data has no reason, reason is null and a note says so; nothing is guessed. Read-only.

prefix.description: Prefix, e.g. 8.8.8.0/24 (the length may be omitted when unambiguous)

vrf.description: VRF, only needed when the prefix is in several VRFs

name: list_routers
description: List the routers in a network-xray lab state and which protocols have state for each (ospf: OSPF neighbors or LSDB in the data; bgp: BGP neighbors or BGP routes), whether a routing table was collected, and row counts. Read-only.

name: ospf_neighbors
description: OSPF neighbors per router as collected: neighbor router ID, address, state (e.g. Full), interface, and DR/BDR role and peer node name when known. All routers, or one with `router`. Read-only.

router.description: Only this router, e.g. r1 (default: all routers)

name: bgp_neighbors
description: BGP neighbors per router as collected: peer address, remote AS, iBGP/eBGP, state, established, and prefixes received (null when the data has no count). All routers, or one with `router`. Read-only.

router.description: Only this router, e.g. r1 (default: all routers)

name: route_lookup
description: Look up a destination address in one router's collected routing table (installed rows only) by longest prefix match: the matching route, its protocol, next hop and outgoing interface (all next hops for ECMP). next_hop is null for a directly connected route; route is null with a note when nothing matches. This reads the table the collector saved; it does not compute routing. Read-only.

destination.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address, e.g. 8.8.8.8 or 2001:db8::1 (no prefix length)

vrf.description: VRF of the routing table rows to search (default: the default VRF)

name: why_path
description: Why one router selected its BGP path to a prefix: the selected path, the other candidates with their attributes, the deciding step, and where that reason came from: reason_source "device" when the router reported it (FRR selectionReason), "comparison" when network-xray inferred it by comparing the attributes in the data (Weight, LocPrf, AS-Path, Origin, MED), or null with a note when neither says. A bare address is matched to the longest BGP prefix that contains it. Read-only.

prefix.description: Prefix (e.g. 8.8.8.0/24) or an address inside it (e.g. 8.8.8.8)

vrf.description: VRF, only needed when the prefix is in several VRFs
